takeaway: Teratoma: a non-seminomatous germ cell tumour of many cell types; a hard testicular lump in a young man with a positive beta-hCG.

question.text: A 25-year-old man discovers a hard lump on his left testicle. His GP has arranged a blood test (β-hCG) which is positive. Select the likely diagnosis.
question.say: A twenty-five-year-old man discovers a hard lump on his left testicle. His GP arranges a beta-hCG blood test, which is positive. What is the likely diagnosis?

lines.say: This twenty-five-year-old man has just found something worrying.

lines.text: A hard lump in his left testicle.
lines.say: It is a hard lump in his left testicle.
His beta-hCG blood test comes back positive.

lines.text: A teratoma is made of many cell types.
lines.say: (laugh) Meet the teratoma, a tumour made of many cell types, with tooth, hair, bone and muscle all mixed together.

lines.text: They come from one or more of the three germ layers.
lines.say: These cells come from one or more of the three germ layers, from abnormal pluripotent cells.

lines.text: It is a non-seminomatous germ cell tumour.
lines.say: Teratomas belong to the non-seminomatous germ cell tumours.

lines.text: Remember: a hard testicular lump with a positive beta-hCG suggests teratoma.
lines.say: Remember: a hard testicular lump in a young man with a positive beta-hCG suggests teratoma.
